record.paper_title: Open problems in combinatorial group theory
record.original_question: Given a finite presentation of a hyperbolic group that is not necessarily a Dehn presentation, can one find a Dehn presentation for the group in polynomial time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A finitely generated group $G$ is called word hyperbolic if its Cayley graph (with respect to some, equivalently any, finite generating set) is a Gromov-hyperbolic metric space. A finite presentation $\langle X \mid R\rangle$ of $G$ is called a Dehn presentation if for every nontrivial word $w$ in $X \cup X^{-1}$ representing the identity in $G$, there exist a relator $r \in R$ (cyclically reduced) and a factorization $r = uv$ such that $w$ contains $u$ as a subword and $|v| < |u|$; equivalently, the word problem can be solved by iteratively replacing such subwords $u$ by $v^{-1}$, strictly decreasing the length at every step. It is a theorem of Gromov that a finitely presented group is word hyperbolic if and only if it admits a Dehn presentation.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input an arbitrary finite presentation $\langle X \mid R\rangle$ of a word hyperbolic group $G$ (not assumed to be a Dehn presentation), produces in time polynomial in the total length of the input a Dehn presentation for $G$?
artifact.status_search_result: No source found that resolves this problem. Related work (e.g., polynomial-time procedures that certify hyperbolicity and produce linear-time word-problem solvers when they succeed) addresses adjacent algorithmic questions but does not establish a polynomial-time algorithm to convert an arbitrary finite presentation of a hyperbolic group into a Dehn presentation. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial-time proofs that groups are hyperbolic
status_evidence.snippet: A polynomial-time procedure either returns an explicit linear Dehn function for the presentation, or returns fail, together with its reasons for failure.
status_evidence.claim: There exist polynomial-time procedures that succeed in proving hyperbolicity for some presentations but may fail; no general polynomial-time conversion to a Dehn presentation is established.

status_evidence.title: Dehn function - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A finitely presented group is word hyperbolic if and only if it admits a Dehn presentation.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the equivalence used in the problem statement.
